Orientation: As you continue your journey through Logan International Airport, the Boston Logan Airport History Walk at Terminal E offers a reflective space.

 The plane made an emergency landing at Logan, preventing disaster and prompting enhanced security measures worldwide. Reid’s failed attempt serves as a stark reminder of the vigilance necessary in modern air travel, influencing global airport security protocols. The disappearance of Walter and passengers on that ill-fated flight, added a layer of mystery and tragedy to Logan history. The incident spurred safety reviews and advancements in runway technology, ensuring better preparation against harsh weather conditions. In September 1968, the Maverick Street Mothers, a group of local mothers, stood up against the airport's expansion by blocking dump trucks. Their protest led to changes in airport policies, highlighting the power of community activism.
